It closes a question once you have clearly answered it and doesn't ask it again.

What the requirement says: an item counts as answered only if the last reply showed it, at that version, and your message talks about it. Example EX-7 shows the strict side of this: if you say "the export one is fine too" and the export item wasn't shown, it is not taken as answered.

What changed: plumb now also counts a record as answerable when an open review question asked you about it, at the version it asked about, even if the last reply didn't show it. A typed answer to that question is read the same way as an answer to a shown record. The question is then closed or asked again in a new form, never repeated word for word.

What's unclear: this fits your wish that a clear answer to a question closes it. But it widens the requirement's rule that only shown items can be answered. It also means a case like EX-7 would be taken as answered if an open question had asked about the export item. What changed: the landing job's commit step now has its own filter. It builds paths starting with ".plumb/log/" and checks the log kind's name to leave out segments of kinds kept local. The goal is reasonable. A local kind's segment is ignored by git, and naming it would make the whole commit fail. That ties in with keeping local kinds unstaged. But putting the check in the landing job means the landing job now knows and names the log folder, which your decision rules out.

The prompt logged just before the change was about something else (which host list a merge keeps), and it didn't ask for this. The fix is ordinary development work with no question for you: move the filtering into the log module. For example, the log module could give the landing job the list of log paths that are safe to commit, or commit them itself.
